node.title: N=256 proper-conductor E1 collision exclusion
node.statement: For either first-band N=256,s=5 folded profile (4,2,0) or (3,4,0), let T be the actual nonzero support. If d=gcd(256,{i-r:i in T})>1, monomial normalization places the vector in a cyclotomic subfield of degree at most 64. Its nonzero small-field norm has magnitude at most 18^32<2^250, while the full norm is a power of that same integer up to sign. Hence no pair-feasible row prime divides it, and every unresolved first-band collision has full conductor. A certified profile-(3,4,0) vector of variance 36 shows that low variance does not imply proper conductor.
node.notes: ROUTE REDUCTION 2026-07-27: removes every proper-subfield lift from both first-band N=256 profiles. Full-conductor vectors remain in the low-variance residual, so neither profile nor the total ledger is closed.
